newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks rebound in early trade, property counters lead.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks rebound in early trade, property counters lead.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumped 153 points or 1.22 percent to 12,694 in early Monday morning trade due to a rebound in shares of property developers.
The index then eased to trade 141 points higher at 12,682 after 50 minutes. Turnover was HK$1.77 million.
Brokers said Wall Street was a major factor in the gains, with the Dow industrials gaining more than 300 points over the last week.
They said local factors were also helping Hong Kong shares, including "1997 fever".
"Everybody who's going to be here after July has a vested interest in making sure that it is seen to be strong," said a trader in institutional sales at a regional brokerage.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule.
The sharp rise in the index defied the predictions of brokers who had expected interest rate fears to keep blue chips range-bound, including property stocks.
The market has had problems sustaining gains above the 12,600-point level in recent weeks.
Brokers expected buying interest in H shares and red chips.
Cheerful Research Co said in a report that it expected continued trading volatility and warned investors to be cautious.
Trading in shares of H-share company Jilin Chemical, expected to announce results later in the day, was suspended in the morning at the company's request.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd led the gainers, leaping HK$2.25 to HK$80.50, followed by Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd, which rose HK$1.75 to HK$69.
New World Development Co Ltd rose HK$1.30 to HK$41.10, and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd rose HK$1.25 to HK$66.
HSBC Holdings Plc was HK$1 firmer at HK$187.50, and subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd was up HK$1.50 at HK$84.50.
